title: AI finds 44 star systems that could hide Earth-like planets
key_facts: University of Bern and the PlanetS national research centre built a machine-learning model (random forest of 500 trees); study in Astronomy & Astrophysics; Jeanne Davoult developed it.
Trained on tens of thousands of simulated systems from the Bern Model of Planet Formation and Evolution.
Precision up to 99% on simulated systems (94% for the lowest-mass stars).
Applied to 1,567 observed systems: 51 got over 90% of tree votes; 7 binary systems excluded, leaving 44.
A preliminary stability check found room for an extra planet in 42 of 44 systems.
Earth-like defined as 0.5 to 3 Earth masses and equilibrium temperature 160 to 510 K.
Limits: the simulation makes too many planets close to stars; predictions are unconfirmed.
quote_evidence: The model reached precision scores of up to 99% when tested on simulated planetary systems. That result measures performance within a computer-generated population.
The predicted worlds around actual stars remain unconfirmed, and the method's value will depend on follow-up observations.
The calculation supports the possibility of additional planets; it does not demonstrate that they exist or guarantee their long-term stability.
why_it_matters_hint: The list could help astronomers choose where to spend scarce telescope time.
event_date: Study date not stated; article 4 Oct 2026
